A Delta flight departing Boston Logan International Airport was delayed Friday after a cat escaped its kennel and got loose in the cabin, an airlines spokesperson confirmed.
Delta Flight 2706 was headed to Tampa, Florida. The flight resumed after the cat was safely secured and departed normally, the airline said.
Audio of the exchange between the pilot and air traffic control circulated on social media.
“Thanks for accommodating,” the pilot said. “We had a cat loose in the cabin.”
“That is a new one,” the air traffic control person responded. “… Have a good day. Meow.”
Despite the minor delay, the flight arrived in Tampa on time, Delta said.

sources.news_title: A Cat Got Loose on a Delta Flight and Air Traffic Control Had the Perfect Response
sources.text:
In the great 1983 Carl Reiner film, The Man With Two Brains, Steve Martin played the brilliant brain surgeon, Dr. Michael Hfuhruhurr, who has invented the "cranial screw-top" method of entry into the skull. In that film, every time Martin is depicted as conducting a sensitive brain operation in a sterile surgical suite, there is the sound of a meow, and Martin snaps, "Get that cat out of here!"
Passengers and crew on a recent Delta Airlines flight may have felt much the same way when their Boston-Tampa flight was delayed by a cat that had broken out of its travel kennel.
A flight from Boston to Tampa was briefly delayed Friday when a cat escaped its kennel while the aircraft was taxiing before takeoff, according to Delta Air Lines. https://t.co/UpCIpRbhxR
— WTOL 11 (@WTOL11Toledo) November 22, 2026
The cat was quickly recaptured and the flight proceeded.
A Delta Air Lines flight from Boston, Massachusetts, to Tampa, Florida, was briefly delayed Friday when a cat escaped its kennel while the aircraft was taxiing before takeoff.
A spokesperson with Delta Air Lines said the flight was preparing to depart from Logan International Airport at 7 a.m. ET Friday, Nov. 20, when the feline escaped.
"We got a situation in the cabin. We need to hold somewhere for a minute," the captain was heard advising air traffic control.
The plane halted on the taxiway while the cat was secured back in its kennel.
It should come as no surprise that no airline crew would want to taxi, much less take off, with a loose animal on board. That's why there are certain requirements for these things. I've seen people travel with medium-sized dogs that were not in a kennel, although they were required to be leashed. In fact, I've seen a few people traveling with dogs that were better-behaved than many people's children.
Cats, though, have that stubborn independent streak that makes them a little more problematic to be wandering around loose in a passenger airliner, especially during takeoff.
Fortunately, this situation was resolved quickly, and not without a spot of humor from the air traffic controller.
"Thanks for accommodating," the captain said. "We had a cat loose in the cabin."
"That's a new one," the controller responded with a chuckle. He then added, "And have a good day, meow."
The flight resumed taxiing and departed without an issue. The flight arrived on time in Tampa.
It's good to see the air traffic controller keeping his composure, and even dropping some humor. And here's the thing; it wasn't all that long ago, before the FAA and the airlines started reining in the nonsense, that you saw people bringing "emotional support animals," like turkeys, peacocks, snakes, bandicoots, anteaters, you name it. I personally saw a guy who was stopped and not allowed to board with his pot-bellied pig, a porker which had to be 300 pounds, that he insisted was his emotional support pig. Thankfully the United Airlines gate staff said they didn't give a ham, and that the pig wasn't going to be allowed a-boar-d.
A cat, in a travel kennel, now that doesn't seem unreasonable. Just make sure the cat isn't smarter than the latch on the kennel.

sources.news_title: Why was a Delta flight to Tampa held on the Boston taxiway?
sources.text:
A Delta flight bound for Tampa was briefly held on the taxiway at Boston Logan International Airport on Friday morning after a cat got loose in the cabin, as reported by the New York Post. The pilot reached out to air traffic control to report “a situation in the cabin” while the plane was taxiing for takeoff.
The controller told the flight to pull straight ahead and wait before a taxiway called Foxtrot, and asked whether the crew needed help, per A-Z Animals. The pilot said assistance was not needed, so the plane stayed put while the crew dealt with the loose pet.
After a few minutes, the pilot contacted air traffic control again to get back in line for departure. The pilot explained the delay in audio shared in an Instagram video, saying, “Thanks for accommodating, we had a cat loose in the cabin.”
The controller could not resist a cat pun
The controller responded, “That is a new one.” Before handing the flight over to the tower, the controller finished the exchange by saying, “You have a good day, meow.” The audio of the interaction was obtained by Aviation Circle.
A Delta representative told NBC Boston that the pet got outside its kennel, which caused the brief pause on the taxiway. The outlet said it was not clear how the cat was caught.
Once the cat was secured, the flight continued on its way to Florida. The plane took off about 15 minutes late, according to Portland, Maine, station WMTW, as cited by A-Z Animals. Despite the delay on the tarmac, it still arrived in Tampa on time, a Delta spokesperson confirmed to the Post.
Delta allows pets on board, but the rules are strict about keeping animals inside a kennel at all times. Its pet travel policy allows small dogs, cats, and household birds in the cabin on domestic flights, and it requires them to stay in their kennel at the airport, on the aircraft, and in Sky Clubs.
The kennel must fit fully under the seat in front of the passenger, and Delta charges a one-way fee of $150 for in-cabin pets on flights within the US. The airline also limits pets to two in Delta First and four in Delta Comfort and Main on domestic flights. Passengers who break its pet rules may lose the ability to fly with their pet in the future.

A Florida-bound Delta Air Lines flight was briefly delayed on the tarmac at Boston’s Logan International Airport on Friday morning after an unexpected passenger caused a commotion inside the plane. As the aircraft was taxiing for takeoff, the pilot abruptly radioed air traffic control to request a hold over an unusual "situation in the cabin." It turned out that a pet cat had slipped out of its kennel and was roaming loose on board, prompting the crew to pause departure until the animal was safely secured.

sources.news_title: Delta flight delayed on runway at Boston Airport due to a cat
Loose cat causes commotion on flight leaving Logan Airport
sources.text:
Quick Take
- A pilot radioed about "a situation in the cabin" and the jet just sat there. What was it? Hear the radio call →
- A cat's skeleton has a quirk that makes a carrier door a flimsy barrier. See how cats squeeze out →
- Of all the moments to bolt, a taxiing jet is the worst. Cats sense something here that you can't. Why taxiing terrifies cats →
- Ground control had one parting line for the crew. It's the best pun of the day. Read the parting pun →
On Friday morning, November 20, the pilot of Delta Flight 2706 got on the radio from a taxiway at Boston Logan International Airport. The pilot told ground control there was “a situation in the cabin” and asked to stop somewhere for a minute. Ground control told the jet to roll straight ahead and wait before a taxiway called Foxtrot, and offered to help. No help was needed. The jet pulled over and sat there.
A cat had got out of its carrier.
The flight was headed from Boston to Tampa. The cat slipped out while the plane was taxiing for takeoff, an airline spokesperson told WFXT (Boston 25 News), which reported the story and reviewed the air traffic control recording. After a few minutes the pilot asked to get back in line, and the plane took off normally, about 15 minutes late by the count of WMTW, a station in Portland, Maine.
Back in line, the pilot told the controller what had happened. “Thanks for accommodating, we had a cat loose in the cabin.” The controller’s answer: “That is a new one.”
Getting Out Is the Easy Part
A cat can squeeze through a gap that looks far too small for its body. Its collarbones are held in place by muscle instead of being locked to the rest of the skeleton, so its shoulders can fold in and follow its head through. As long as the head fits, the rest of the body usually fits too. Its bendy backbone helps as well: a cat can twist the front and back halves of its body in opposite directions at the same time.
Why a Taxiway Is the Worst Possible Moment
A taxiing jet is loud, and a cat hears more of that noise than any passenger does. A cat’s hearing reaches pitches of about 85,000 vibrations a second, against a person’s 20,000. Loud, unpredictable noise that keeps coming puts a cat’s body on high alert and floods it with stress hormones. A plane rolling toward the runway doesn’t give it a break.
When a situation feels dangerous, a cat’s instinct is to tuck itself away, because hiding is how cats make themselves feel safe. The crew got this one safely secured, and only then did Flight 2706 carry on toward the runway.
What It Sounded Like From Outside
Whatever the scramble looked like between the seats, on the radio it sounded like an ordinary morning of taxiing. Turn right, roll along taxiways Foxtrot and Hotel, stop short of runway 33 Left. Then ground control passed the flight over to the tower, with one parting line.
“You have a good day meow.”

sources.news_title: Cat Escapes Carrier, Delays Delta Flight at Boston Airport
sources.text:
A cat escaped from its carrier and began wandering among passengers, forcing a Delta Air Lines flight to stop taxiing at Boston Logan International Airport on Friday, Nov. 20.
Flight 2706, bound for Tampa, Florida, was delayed for about 15 minutes after the animal got loose inside the cabin. It was around 7 a.m., and the aircraft was approaching the runway for takeoff when the cat managed to escape its carrier.
The crew alerted the captain, who contacted air traffic control to request permission to stop.
“We have a situation in the cabin. We need to stop somewhere for a minute,” the pilot said, without initially explaining what had happened.
The exchange with air traffic control
A recording of the radio communications, shared on social media and picked up by U.S. broadcasters, captured the unusual exchange between the pilot and an air traffic controller.
After receiving permission to stop, the crew managed to retrieve the cat and return it to its carrier. The pilot then requested clearance to resume taxiing and explained the reason for the interruption.
“Thanks for the help. We had a cat loose in the cabin,” he said.
The controller, apparently surprised, replied: “That’s a new one!”
Before ending the exchange, the controller wished the crew a good flight and added an amused “Meow!”
The recording quickly attracted attention from local news outlets and spread across social media.
Flight arrives on time despite 15-minute delay
Despite the interruption, the aircraft departed without further problems and arrived in Tampa on schedule, according to a Delta Air Lines spokesperson.
Neither the passengers nor the animal were harmed, and the cat completed the journey safely inside its carrier.
Delta allows passengers to bring pets into the cabin, provided they remain inside approved carriers throughout the flight, from boarding until deplaning. The requirement is intended to protect passengers, crew members and animals.
On this occasion, the unexpected passenger caused only a brief delay and gave the air traffic controller an unusual opportunity to end a routine exchange with two words: “Meow!”

The flight reached Tampa on schedule

NBC Boston also reported that a Delta representative confirmed the pet had gotten outside its kennel.
